mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in the federal funds rate above 4% over the prior quarter is interpreted by market participants as a signal of tightening financial conditions, which reduces the present value of future earnings for large-cap firms, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases by more than 0.25% in a consecutive monthly pattern for 3 months
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the identified tightening phase (p > 0.05 in a two-tailed test).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate falls below 4.5% for two consecutive months, labor market strength is interpreted as a bullish signal for equities, driving a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4.5% and remains below for at least 2 months
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative or statistically insignificant (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly retail sales (HOUST) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates shifting demand composition toward consumer goods at the expense of capital goods, which is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 3% while INDPRO decreases by at least 2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative or the IC is below 0.05 with p-value < 0.05 in a rolling window of 12 months.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly expansion in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three months suggests improving supply chain dynamics, which anticipates a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is negative and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly rises by more than 0.5% in a month, it is interpreted as a signal of future inflationary pressure, which reduces the real value of equity earnings and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the monthly payrolls growth (PAYEMS) below -0.5% for two consecutive months suggests weakening labor demand, which is associated with a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases by more than 0.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is not negative or the IC is above 0.10 with p-value > 0.05.
